vocabulary.definition: one who has a scholarly viewpoint based on higher learning
a joining together of countries in friendship for the mutual benefit of all members.
to absorb a territory into one's own
ment: a policy of satisfying the demands or giving in to the actions of an aggressor nation in order to avoid war.
a policy of satisfying the demands or giving in to the actions of an aggressor nation in order to avoid war.
a truce or ceasefire during a war
the act of wearing the other side down
blind submission to the state
independent of the laws of another state or government; self-governing
a document that outlines the purpose, structure, and rules of an organization
the safety (security) of the group (collective)

a political, social, and economic theory in which the community or the state owns all property, controls the production and distribution of goods and services, and, to a great extent, controls the social and cultural life of the people. At first, there would be only one political party running the government and no oppossition parties. The goal was to liberate the working classes (for example, labourers in factories, farmers) and build a society with no economic or social classes. There would be no private property. No rich and no poor. Everyone would be equal. Eventually, in the final stages (never reached in practice) there would be no need for government.
compulsory military service
the process of allowing a colony to become self-governing or independent
a leader who obtains power by means of impassioned appeals to the emotions and prejudices of the people
a ruler with absolute power and authority
the process of countries speaking to one another to make agreements peacefully with each other.
a male monarch, usually the sovereign ruler of an empire or another type of imperial realm
a foreigner living in a country where a state of war exists between that citizen's home country and the country in which he/she is living
volunteering to join the military
a nation's practice or policy of territorial or economic expansion
a political and economic system in which the government has complete control over society
fascism: a political and economic system in which the government has complete control over society
a list of new terms that you will encounter in this lesson. Click on each one for a definition:
help provided to nations in need
the methods a country uses while dealing with other countries

the planned, systematic destruction of a certain group of people. According to the UN, genocide is any of the following acts committed with intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnical, racial or religious group, as such:
the genocide of European Jews and others by the Nazis during World War II
someone guided more by visionary ideals than by practical considerations
a theory or concept about the way in which society should be organized
(or colonialism) the purpose or process of a dominant country extending its control over another, weaker country or territory
to teach someone systematically to accept a doctrine or opinion uncritically
persistent increase in the level of consumer prices or a persistent decline in the purchasing power of money
literally, "between nations." Anything between nations. Usually used in reference to nation states rather than other definitions of "nation".

The doctrine that all members of the global community accept collective responsibility for the challenges that face the world and that the motives of nations and nation-states must be respected in the search for solutions. Some may see it as placing global concerns before a country's own national interests, or the best way to protect national interests.
the imprisonment or confinement of people without trial, commonly in large groups
the foreign policy of intervening in the affairs of another country
ism: a policy of non-involvement in international affairs
a policy of non-involvement in international affairs
isolationism: a policy of non-involvement in international affairs
November 9, 1938; German for “night of broken glass”; referred to all the broken glass caused by the breaking of windows in Jewish shops

pursuit of national interests through a policy of aggression and building large armed forces - army, navy, air force. Military officers typically have significant influence in government decision making.
the act of a country calling up its armed forces and preparing them for war
a state of individual psychological well-being based upon a sense of confidence and usefulness and purpose
the policy of pursueing agreements, discussions or negotiations between multiple countries (3 or more).
an independent (self-governing) nation within clearly defined borders that are internationally recognized.
aspects that a particular nation views as important to achieve internationally
the feelings people have in identifying with their nation
ideology of the National Socialist Party (Nazi Party) of Germany whose leader was Adolf Hitler
the policy of not taking sides or entering into alliances.
the foreign policy of not getting involved in the affairs of other countries
the belief that disputes between nations should and can be settled peacefully
one who is opposed to war or violence as a means of resolving disputes

aims to end an active conflict between two parties by using the armed forces of a third country, or coalition of countries, to impose peace. Peace enforcement troops would be more heavily armed than peacekeepers. Unlike peacekeeping, permission from the host country is not necessary in peace-enforcement, especially if human rights or civilians are at risk. Peace-enforcement troops can conduct offensive operations.
immediately after an armed conflict has ended, soldiers from other countries are placed between the aggressive groups to observe and maintain the peace process.

A policy of preventing armed conflict through diplomacy. While peacekeeping aims to keep opposing sides away from each other after an armed conflict, "peacemaking" aims to prevent armed conflict through diplomacy. Peacemaking diplomacy is also used after an armed conflict has been stopped in order to negotiate a permanent peace agreement.
statements, printed materials, posters, radio and television broadcasts, and movies designed to convince people of some point of view

Putting tariffs (taxes) on imported goods to make them more expensive so that your own goods will seem cheaper and sell better. As well, quotas may be created to limit how much of an import comes into your country. This will also help to keep import prices high, which will protect goods made in your country. It’s all done to make people want to buy goods made in their own country which is intended to protect local industries and jobs.
payment for war damages
an individual or group blamed for something when the fault actually lies elsewhere
the freedom of a nation to make its own decisions independent of outside influences from other countries; similar to sovereignty
a country that is free from control by any other country
a chess term meaning that neither side can win
is foreign assistance (money) given by one country to a second country on condition the money is spent in the country giving the aid.
extreme nationalism, especially when opposed to international cooperation
an international organization whose aims are to foster global cooperation in international law, international peace and security, economic development, social progress and human rights issues.
[zen-uh-foh-bee-uh] an unreasonable fear, distrust, or hatred of strangers, foreigners, or anything perceived as foreign or different
